title: Golden eval task
description: One golden eval task for a function-definition package. No prior format existed anywhere in the repo, so this schema is the canonical definition. A task states an input, an expectation (expected_output for generative functions, verdict for judgement functions), and a non-empty rubric of discrete, checkable pass/fail conditions.

id.description: Stable task id, unique within the package. Reported verbatim when a task fails.

description.description: What this task is holding the function to.

input.description: Input payload conforming to the package's own schema.json input shape.

expected_output.description: Expected output shape for a generative function. Rubric entries, not deep equality, decide pass/fail.

verdict.description: Expected judgement for a QA/gating function.

pass.description: Whether the function under test must judge the input as passing.

violations.description: Violation codes the function must emit, e.g. uncleared-client-reference.

rubric.description: Non-empty list of discrete, checkable grading conditions. Every entry must be decidable identically by two independent graders (AC-18, enforced by lint_rubrics.py).

criterion.description: Short label for what is being graded.

condition.description: The discrete pass/fail test, stated so that two graders reach the same verdict. Unqualified subjective terms are rejected by lint_rubrics.py.

check_type.description: tool_check: graded deterministically by the package's own tool_check.py. llm_judged: graded by a grading completion through the model gateway (mocked by default, never a real host).

check.description: Machine-executable form of `condition`. Required so a mocked run is deterministic and a live run has an unambiguous ground truth.

kind.description: Check dispatch key. Generic kinds (contains_all, not_contains, regex, min_words, max_words, min_distinct) are implemented centrally; package-specific kinds are implemented by that package's tool_check.py.

notes.description: Optional free-text provenance note (e.g. which positioning.md section this task is anchored to).
